text:
Jordan Greenway came to Chicago from Buffalo in June in the Bowen Byram trade, and five weeks into the season his name is already in trade talk: a Markerzone headline says Elliotte Friedman linked him to the market. The numbers explain the restlessness. He has one point in 17 games and none in his last 16, and the Blackhawks have just 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he's out there.

Nobody brought him in for points. He's a 6'6" forward with 34 hits, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his game was never built on creating offense at five on five. The trouble is that the chances have thinned out too, his ice time is down two minutes over his last ten games, and Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level last season, on a small sample. Now comes a twist. The Athletic's Scott Powers reports Greenway filling in for Tyler Bertuzzi on the top line with Connor Bedard. That's the audition to watch.
